args.content: Clause 13.3 governs valuation. It says variations are valued by measurement of the change in quantities using BOQ rates only where the work is of similar character and executed under similar conditions; a new rate is agreed only where no similar item exists. On your facts, kerb removal and re-laying has no BOQ rate, so it should be treated as a new rate under clause 13.3 rather than priced from an existing BOQ line unless a genuinely similar BOQ item exists. Clause 13.4 also means no percentage addition for preliminaries or overheads.

args.content: This is a valid Variation if the Engineer instructs it or confirms it by revised drawing, because clause 13.1 allows Variations before completion and clause 1.1 defines a Variation as a change instructed under clause 13. The valuation basis is clause 13.3: measure the change in quantities and use BOQ rates where the work is of similar character and similar conditions; a new rate is only for any item with no similar BOQ item. Clause 13.4 bars any percentage add-on for preliminaries or overheads, and the contract says rates already include preliminaries, overheads and profit. For time, clause 8.4 allows EOT only to the extent completion is delayed by the Variation, assessed on the current programme by critical path and float; clause 8.5 then pays time-related costs only if EOT is granted, at AED 2,500 [F-0944] per working day of extension granted, with no other time-related costs. Acceleration is only if the Employer instructs it under clause 8.6, with AED 3,000 [F-0945] mobilisation per additional crew per activity and AED 1,800 [F-0946] per crew per working day, and no more than one additional crew on any single activity. Notice: clause 20.1 requires notice within 28 [F-0947] days of becoming aware of the event for additional payment or EOT. Design: clause 4.1 says structural design is the Employer’s design consultant’s responsibility; the road widening appears to raise a design/check question only if the revised kerb line or road geometry affects structural or design-coordination matters, so that should be checked against the design team rather than assumed.

payload.content:
To all — ASSESS

The road widening change adds duration to five critical-path activities: A100, A110, A120, A140 and A150 each increase by 1 [F-0344] working day, for a total added duration of 5 [F-0376] working days. On the current programme, completion remains at working day 92 [F-0387] and 2027-02-09 [F-0388], with the same critical path through A920 [F-0387]. That means this change does not delay completion on the present float position; A160 still has 15 [F-0458] working days float, and the non-road packages retain float as shown in the CPM.

Contractually, clause 8.4 gives extension of time only if the Variation delays completion, and clause 8.5 makes time-related costs payable only if an extension is granted, at AED 2,500 [F-0950] per working day of extension. On this programme run, I do not see a delay to completion, so no extension of time is shown on the current facts. Clause 20.1 notice remains 28 [F-0951] days.
